To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sublethally toxic Cd concentrations are stressful for carp, particularly with respect to the branchial enzymes which can disrupt the osmoregulatory function of the fish.

Cd exposure to juvenile carp resulted in a significant inhibition of branchial (Na(+), K(+)) ATPase activity, a significant activation of branchial Mg(2+), ATPase activity, and a significant increase of GOT and GPT activity in liver.
Cd exposure in juvenile carp resulted in significant changes in gill ATPases and liver transaminase activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a long-term Cd exposure to carp and the effects on selected biomarkers of toxicity.
the effects of waterborne Cd on the fish C. carpio.
the use of biomarkers of exposure and effect to evaluate sublethal toxicity of Cd in juvenile C. carpio.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cd-induced changes in the biomarkers are not reversible after the 19 days recovery phase.
Cd exposure to C. carpio induces a series of alterations in the fish, and that these alterations are reversible in most of the cases, but in some of them, they are irreversible.
the long-term exposure to sublethal Cd levels in water induces changes in the activity of some biomarkers of toxicity and that the recovery of the fish after Cd removal is not complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd is a toxicant that affects the physiology of carp and the biomarkers measured in this study may be used to monitor its effects in fish.
the Cd exposure caused an alteration of gill function, which was not completely reversible after 19 days of recovery.
the Cd exposure caused a general stress to the carp, which was reflected in changes of some biomarkers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of biomarkers in fish may provide valuable information for the evaluation of the impact of Cd on aquatic organisms and may be useful in the monitoring of water quality.
biomarkers can be used to evaluate the effects of environmental contaminants and to predict the potential risks to aquatic organisms.
Cd exposure induces a significant increase in the liver GOT and GTP activities which can be used as biomarkers of Cd exposure.
